LESSON: DRAWING AND PAINTING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.1: Drawing and Painting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Drawing and Painting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are complimentary colours?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss dominance in a picture
2. classify complementary colours on a colour wheel
3. appreciate own and others pictures

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DRAWING AND PAINTING
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Drawing and Painting helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DRAWING AND PAINTING
Study Drawing and Painting like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss dominance in a picture

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss dominance in a picture. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss dominance in a picture.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Drawing and Painting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss dominance in a picture. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Classify complementary colours on a colour wheel

What this means
In this part you learn to classify complementary colours on a colour wheel. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify complementary colours on a colour wheel.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Drawing and Painting in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify complementary colours on a colour wheel. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate own and others pictures

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate own and others pictures. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate own and others pictures.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate own and others pictures. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Drawing and Painting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Drawing and Painting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss dominance in a picture)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Drawing and Painting in your own words. (skill: classify complementary colours on a colour wheel)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate own and others pictures)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Drawing and Painting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss dominance in a picture.
3. Practise this skill: classify complementary colours on a colour wheel.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate own and others pictures.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Drawing and Painting from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Drawing and Painting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Drawing and Painting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are complimentary colours?
2. How is dominance created using in a picture?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Drawing and Painting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss dominance in a picture.
5. Be able to: classify complementary colours on a colour wheel.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
